raw_case_text:
A 50s male patient with cough, bloody sputum expectoration, slight fever and slightly visible body rashes at the thoracoabdominal junction (Figure 1A) presented to Zhejiang Provincial People's Hospital on July 6, 2021 because of pulmonary shadow found in physical examination of local hospital for more than half a year. The patient had been healthy and had not been infected with HIV in the past but had a 30-year history of smoking. After admission, the physical examination was completed. The body temperature was 37.6 C, pulse rate was 105 times/min, respiration was 20 times/min, blood pressure was 101/68 mmHg, and the breath sound was coarse through auscultation of both lungs. The results of the initial laboratory examination are shown in Table 1. In addition, we also monitored the laboratory test indicators of patients during hospitalization (Figure 2A-D). Chest computed tomography (CT) showed pulmonary solid mass in the right upper lobe with apical bronchial occlusion, patchy infiltration and irregular thickening of local interlobular septum. There were multiple nodules, patchy and cord infiltration in the right lower lobe with fuzzy boundary, irregular thickening of interlobular septum and adjacent pleural thickening. Fibrous foci and tiny nodules were seen in the left lower lobe, presenting with a right pleural effusion (Figure 3A; July 8th). 
No cancer cells were found in fibrobronchoscopic fluid, pleural effusion or pulmonary masses and no abnormal cells were seen by bone marrow biopsy. The histopathological results of the right pulmonary masses showed multifocal areas of consolidation with fibrous polypoid tissue, alveolar epithelium and vascular hyperplasia in the alveolar cavity. A large number of lymphocytes, plasma cells, phagocytes and neutrophils were infiltrated in the lung tissue, and the pulmonary septum was widened, which suggested that chronic active inflammation of lung tissue with parenchymal lesions and bronchiolitis obliterans with organized pneumonia (BOOP) (Figure 1B-F).
Tuberculosis screening laboratory demonstrated negative acid-fast staining in a suppurative inflammatory background with plentiful neutrophils and macrophages, which preliminarily ruled out the infection of Mycobacterium (Figure 4B). Blue fluorescent fungal spores were observed in the dark field indicating fungal infection by fungal fluorescence staining of sputum (Figure 4C). Gram staining of alveolar lavage fluid showed that deeply stained fungal spores were detected (Figure 4D). Scattered, slightly asymmetric and typical double-helical broom-like fungal hyphae with short, smooth walled, ellipsoidal, mono-verticillate penicillium conidiophores were observed under oil lens after gently touching scotch tape to the colonies and staining with lactophenol cotton blue (Figure 4E). Fungal culture of BALF revealed colonies with temperature-dependent dimorphic growth character, which showed yeast-like fungi producing soluble red pigment at 28 C and mycelia at 37 C in CANA, PDA and SDA (Figure 4F). Single band PCR amplification for internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region in genomic DNA of the clinical isolate was observed after electrophoresis (Figure 4A). The nucleotide sequences of the 563-bp ITS including the 5.8S rRNA and 26S rRNA gene were verified and utilized to perform phylogenetic analysis by the Molecular Evolutionary Genetics Analysis (MEGA) software version 11 through the minimum-evolution method as reported in the previous literature. A phylogenetic tree was constructed utilizing the sequence of Talaromyces marneffei ZJPPH1 (GenBank number: ON287261.1) from the isolate of this study along with 53 available sequences with the highest homology retrieved from GenBank. The nucleic acid sequence of the present isolate revealed 99.62% similarity with Talaromyces marneffei strain AMC PM002 (Figure 5).

subjective.chief_complaint: A male patient in his 50s presented on July 6, 2021 with cough, bloody sputum expectoration, low-grade fever, a thoracoabdominal rash, and a pulmonary shadow noted for over 6 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A pulmonary mass/shadow had been detected on routine examination at a local hospital more than 6 months prior to presentation; he subsequently presented with cough, hemoptysis/blood-streaked sputum, mild fever, and a faint thoracoabdominal rash.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy with no history of HIV infection; 30-year history of cigarette smoking.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for cough, bloody sputum, mild fever, and thoracoabdominal skin rash.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: temperature 37.6 °C, pulse 105 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, and blood pressure 101/68 mmHg. Cutaneous inspection showed a faint rash at the thoracoabdominal junction. Chest auscultation revealed coarse breath sounds bilaterally.
objective.routine_investigations: HIV testing was negative. Sputum acid-fast bacilli (AFB) staining was negative against a suppurative background of neutrophils and macrophages, whereas sputum fungal fluorescence staining revealed blue fluorescent fungal spores.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT (July 8, 2021) demonstrated a solid mass in the right upper lobe with apical bronchial occlusion, patchy infiltrates, and interlobular septal thickening; multiple nodules and patchy/cord-like infiltrates with adjacent pleural thickening in the right lower lobe; fibrous foci and tiny nodules in the left lower lobe; and a right pleural effusion. Cytology of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, pleural effusion, and lung mass as well as bone marrow biopsy were negative for malignancy. Right lung mass histopathology showed multifocal consolidation with fibrous polypoid tissue, alveolar epithelial and vascular hyperplasia, dense lymphocytic/plasmacytic/neutrophilic/macrophage infiltration, and bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP) changes.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Pulmonary talaromycosis with secondary bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP) in an HIV-negative male smoker. Definitive pathogen confirmation was achieved via Gram stain of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) showing deeply stained fungal spores, BALF culture on CANA, PDA, and SDA media demonstrating thermal dimorphism (yeast-like colonies with soluble red pigment at 28 °C and mycelia with mono-verticillate penicillium conidiophores on lactophenol cotton blue staining at 37 °C), and 563-bp ITS rRNA PCR amplification and sequencing (strain ZJPPH1, GenBank ON287261.1) showing 99.62% sequence homology with Talaromyces marneffei strain AMC PM002. Malignancy and Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection were ruled out.
